questions.q: In a running show, which key sequence jumps directly to slide number 7?
questions.solution: Type the slide number and press Enter to jump straight there during a show (works up to the deck's length).
questions.shortcut: Type-and-Enter is the show's hidden navigator; Home/End only reach first/last.

questions.q: Which function displays the current date that updates every time the workbook recalculates?
questions.solution: =TODAY() returns the live current date (updating on recalculation); =NOW() adds the time as well; =DATE() builds a date from given year/month/day; Ctrl+D fills down, it does not insert a date.
questions.shortcut: 'Date only, updating' -> TODAY(); 'date and time' -> NOW(); 'fixed stamp' -> Ctrl+;.

questions.q: Restarting a computer without switching off the power is called:
questions.solution: Warm booting (restart) reloads the OS without removing power. Cold booting means starting from a fully powered-off state.
questions.shortcut: Warm = restart (machine stays 'warm'); cold = switch on from off.

questions.q: The formula =SUM(A1:A5, 10) is entered in B1. A1:A5 contain 2, 4, 6, 8, 10. The result is:
questions.solution: SUM adds the range (2+4+6+8+10 = 30) plus the extra argument 10, giving 40.
questions.shortcut: SUM takes every argument: range total first, then any loose numbers.

questions.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number (1).
questions.solution: 'Every morning' sets habitual present and 'the city' is singular, so the finite verb takes -s: **awakens**. *Awakened* would break the habitual frame, *awaken* lacks agreement, and *awakening* is not a finite verb form.
questions.shortcut: Anchor + skeleton: 'every morning' + 'the city ___' → simple present with -s.
questions.passage: Every morning, before the city fully (1) ______, a quiet crowd gathers in the parks. Retired teachers, young joggers and mothers returning from the dairy booths share the same paths. The morning walk costs nothing and demands no equipment, (2) ______ very few people manage to continue it beyond a fortnight. Doctors point out that its benefits depend almost entirely on (3) ______; twenty minutes on Sunday cannot undo six days of sitting. Over the weeks, a regular walker begins to (4) ______ noticeable changes — lighter steps, deeper sleep and a steadier mood. Perhaps that is why a group that walks together (5) ______ its own quiet discipline: the ones who arrive late feel they have missed something worth keeping.

questions.q:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

Mother said to me, "Do not go out in the rain."
options: Mother said me not to go out in the rain.
Mother told me to not going out in the rain.
Mother told me don't go out in the rain.
Mother told me not to go out in the rain.
questions.solution: Negative command → **told + object + not to + V1**. B uses 'said me'; C breaks the to-structure; D keeps the direct form 'don't'.
questions.shortcut: Negative order skeleton: told + me + not to + go.

questions.q:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

The novel was written by Premchand.
questions.solution: 'was written' → simple past active: **wrote**. B keeps the passive verb; C and D both shift the tense (present perfect, past perfect).

questions.q: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.solution: Independent ends **-ent** (same family as dependent, consistent, persistent). Every distractor swaps the final vowel pair.

questions.q: Which of the following received the **Bharat Ratna in 1954**, the first year of the award?
questions.solution: The 1954 recipients were **C. Rajagopalachari, S. Radhakrishnan and C.V. Raman**. Nehru got it in 1955; Ambedkar and Patel received it posthumously in 1990 and 1991.

questions.q: Tulsidas composed the ***Ramcharitmanas*** in which language?
questions.solution: *Ramcharitmanas* (16th century) is in **Awadhi**. Surdas wrote *Sursagar* in Braj Bhasha; Vidyapati wrote in Maithili.

questions.q: The temperate grasslands of Argentina are known as:
questions.solution: The **Pampas** are the temperate grasslands of **Argentina** (and Uruguay). Prairies are in North America, Steppes in Eurasia and Downs in Australia.

questions.q: The city of **Agra** was founded in 1504 by —
questions.solution: **Sikandar Lodi** founded Agra and made it his second capital. He also introduced the **Gaz-i-Sikandari**, a standard measuring yard.

questions.q: In $\triangle ABC$, $\angle B=55^\circ$ and $\angle C=45^\circ$. If $I$ is the incentre of the triangle, then $\angle BIC$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
$\angle A=180^\circ-55^\circ-45^\circ=80^\circ$.

$\angle BIC=90^\circ+\frac{A}{2}=90^\circ+40^\circ=130^\circ$.

questions.q: A milkman mixes 1 litre of water with every 5 litres of milk and sells the mixture at the cost price of milk. His profit per cent is:
questions.solution: Profit $= \frac{\text{water}}{\text{milk}} \times 100 = \frac{1}{5} \times 100 = 20\%$.
questions.shortcut: Free water per honest litre = profit fraction ⇒ 20%.

questions.q: Two concentric circles have radii $25$ cm and $7$ cm. A chord of the larger circle touches the smaller circle. The length of this chord is:
questions.figure: <svg viewBox="0 0 300 195" width="300" stroke="currentColor" fill="none"><circle cx="150" cy="105" r="68"/><circle cx="150" cy="105" r="19"/><line x1="84.7" y1="86" x2="215.3" y2="86"/><line x1="150" y1="105" x2="215.3" y2="86" stroke-dasharray="4 3"/><text x="150" y="105" dx="4" dy="6" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-size="14" font-family="sans-serif">O</text><text x="84.7" y="86" dx="-14" dy="0" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-size="14" font-family="sans-serif">A</text><text x="215.3" y="86" dx="2" dy="-4" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-size="14" font-family="sans-serif">B</text><text x="150" y="86" dx="-6" dy="-6" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-size="14" font-family="sans-serif">M</text></svg>
questions.solution:
The radius of the smaller circle is the distance from the centre to the chord. Half-chord
$=\sqrt{25^2-7^2}=\sqrt{625-49}=24$, so the chord is $48$ cm.
questions.shortcut: 7-24-25 triplet: half-chord 24 → chord 48 cm. Trap: 24 cm (half only).

questions.q: What is the value of $0.\overline{6} + 0.\overline{7} + 0.\overline{8}$?
questions.shortcut: Adding digits (6 + 7 + 8 = 21 → 2.1) ignores the carries from the endless tail.

questions.q: Find the odd one out: **BDF, HJL, NPR, STV**
questions.solution: Steps: BDF (+2, +2), HJL (+2, +2), NPR (+2, +2), STV (+1, +2) → **STV** breaks the pattern.
questions.shortcut: Step tuples settle cluster odd-one-out in one written line.
questions.pattern: letter-cluster odd one out — step mismatch

questions.q: Select the related cluster: **B3D : E6J :: H12N : ?**
questions.solution: Letters: B→E and D→J are both **+3** (B=2→5=E, D=4→10=J). Number: 3→6 is **×2**. Apply to H12N: H+3 = K, N+3 = Q, 12×2 = 24 → **K24Q**.
questions.shortcut: Mixed clusters: solve the letter track (+3, +3) and the number track (×2) separately, then assemble.

questions.q: How many triangles are there in the given figure?
questions.figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 154 118" width="154" height="118" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><line x1="5" y1="113" x2="149" y2="113"/><line x1="149" y1="113" x2="77" y2="5"/><line x1="77" y1="5" x2="5" y2="113"/><line x1="77" y1="113" x2="77" y2="5"/><line x1="41" y1="59" x2="77" y2="113"/><line x1="77" y1="113" x2="113" y2="59"/></svg>
questions.solution: The vertical line from the apex splits the triangle into 2 halves. Two lines from the base midpoint to the midpoints of the slanted sides cut each half into 2 → 4 smallest. The 2 halves themselves → 2. The whole triangle → 1. Total **7**.

questions.q: Two different positions of the same dice are shown. Which letter is on the face opposite to **Z**? (Ignore the orientation of the letters/numbers.)
questions.figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 124 59" width="124" height="59" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.3" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><polygon points="4,21 38,21 38,55 4,55"/><polygon points="4,21 38,21 55,4 21,4"/><polygon points="38,21 55,4 55,38 38,55"/><text x="21" y="43" font-size="14" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-family="sans-serif">Y</text><text x="29.5" y="16.5" font-size="10" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-family="sans-serif">X</text><text x="46.5" y="33.5" font-size="10" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-family="sans-serif">Z</text><polygon points="69,21 103,21 103,55 69,55"/><polygon points="69,21 103,21 120,4 86,4"/><polygon points="103,21 120,4 120,38 103,55"/><text x="86" y="43" font-size="14" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-family="sans-serif">Y</text><text x="94.5" y="16.5" font-size="10" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-family="sans-serif">W</text><text x="111.5" y="33.5" font-size="10" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-family="sans-serif">V</text></svg>
questions.solution: Y is common and in the **same position** (front) in both views. So faces in matching positions are opposite: top X ↔ top W, right Z ↔ right V. Opposite of Z is **V**.
questions.shortcut: Same position of the common face.
